title: Enhancing professional communication training in higher education through artificial intelligence(AI)-integrated exercises: study protocol for a randomised controlled trial
extended_summary:
This paper is a study protocol for a cluster-randomized controlled trial examining whether AI-supported communication-skills exercises can improve professional communication training in higher education. The problem it addresses is that conventional communication training for future health and psychology professionals is resource-intensive and difficult to scale, while generative AI may offer more accessible, personalized, and repeatable practice opportunities. The paper is explicitly not a results paper: no participant outcome data have been collected for the main trial at the time of publication.

The intervention adds AI-enhanced, text-based communication exercises to teaching-as-usual seminar instruction. Psychology students interact through the HAWKI platform, a GDPR-compliant wrapper around OpenAI ChatGPT/GPT-4o, using structured prompts that simulate communication scenarios and provide feedback. The control condition receives teaching-as-usual only, and some additional non-randomized comparison classes may also be observed. Primary outcome is change in communication skills from baseline to end of seminar; secondary outcomes include self-efficacy, self-concept, motivation, attitudes toward AI, usability, course evaluations, and exercise uptake.

The study population is undergraduate psychology students enrolled in a communication-skills seminar at a single medium-sized university in Germany. Randomization occurs at the seminar-class level to reduce contamination across students within the same class. The protocol also describes a prior pilot phase used to test prompts, feasibility, and instrument development, but those pilot data are not part of the main trial analyses.

The main conclusion of the paper is prospective rather than evidentiary: the authors argue that this trial will provide evidence about the effectiveness and feasibility of integrating generative AI into communication-skills training in higher education. For the verification topic, this paper should not be treated as evidence of ChatGPT effectiveness in high school writing or motivation outcomes. It is not a completed outcome study, not conducted in secondary education, and not focused on writing feedback; therefore it does not provide the original statistics needed to support any extreme effect size claim.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed study protocol, not a completed trial report. No participant outcome data, statistical results, or effect sizes are presented, so it cannot contribute empirical causal evidence to a synthesis of intervention effectiveness.
impact_tier_rationale: Impact is currently unknown because no results are reported. The protocol describes planned outcomes, including motivation and communication skills, but provides no observed effects to classify as positive, null, or negative.

interventions.use_case: ChatGPT/GPT-4o delivered through the HAWKI university wrapper to simulate client/patient communication scenarios for psychology undergraduates, provide iterative text-based practice, model answers, and feedback on motivational interviewing and related communication skills.
Teaching-as-usual seminar exercises without AI, used as the control/comparator condition in communication-skills training.
